chapters.title: The factory question hidden inside an AI project
A graph is not yet manufacturing knowledge
Product, process and resource in depth
OPC UA, AAS and where Microsoft Fabric fits
A practical PPR architecture in layers
Use cases: root cause, prediction and change impact

takeaways: A PPR knowledge graph links product, process and resource facts from ERP, MES, historian and maintenance systems so an operating situation can be reconstructed instead of guessed.
Planned and actual facts must stay separate and the model must preserve effective time, because the same machine, route or product name can mean different things after a revision or tool change.

Standards like ISA-95, OPC UA and the Asset Administration Shell and platforms like Microsoft Fabric provide structure and plumbing, but the PPR semantics still need deliberate mappings from people who know the factory.
hook: Factory AI can read ERP, MES and historian data but still does not know how a product, process and resource came together at one moment. This episode shows manufacturing data architects and plant engineers how a product-process-resource knowledge graph adds that context and enables root cause analysis, prediction and change impact work.
